events.title: A Gift in Motion
events.description: A multidisciplinary showcase from the artists and scholars of the full-time faculty and staff at the Corcoran School of the Arts & Design. A Gift In Motion loosely draws from Robin Wall Kimmerer’s book The Serviceberry which uplifts Indigenous frameworks of the natural world to advance the possibilities in collectivity, reciprocity, and the mindset of abundance. These are anti-capitalist models and theories that provide insight into the systems of power we negotiate, but also offer a lens on how we individually move through our daily lives—together—through historically fraught landscapes. A keen reminder that working with, for, and because of each other remains the most human motivation, even while we are inundated with narratives that suggest otherwise. Within the walls of the academy, frameworks of artistic and creative knowledge are often dismissed, as are Indigenous methodologies and community-focused perspectives that center human engagement, oral and craft-based practices, and unquantifiable research. A personal experience. A feeling. Abstraction. And yet, for centuries, within the walls of art schools exist myriad economies of imagination that are anchored in the sharing of diverse creative knowledge and articulated in what we make, write, perform, dance, build, conserve, collect, display, speak, and think. events.title: Camelot
events.description: Welcome to CAMELOT! Borrowing from the Arthurian legends, CAMELOT is Lerner and Loewe's fantastical masterpiece. An idealistic King Arthur hopes to create a kingdom built on honor and dignity, embodied by his Knights of The Round Table. He establishes an order built on using “might for right.” His ideals, however, are tested when his lovely queen, Guenevere, falls in love with his most loyal knight, Lancelot. Add in the dastardly Mordred and his wicked schemes and it soon appears this dream of a kingdom may only exist for one brief, shining moment. ​ This stirring Golden Age musical has enchanted generations of theatregoers with its sweeping score and iconic characters. It is a romance, a tragedy, a comedy, an adventure, a fantasy, and a stirring exploration of power and leadership all at once. And above all, it is a piece about the stories and ideals we pass along to future generations.​

events.title: Camp One Heartland
events.description: Camp One Heartland is a solo exhibition by Tye DuSold-O’Connor archiving documentation of one of the world’s first nonprofit summer camps designated to supporting and empowering youth affected by HIV and AIDS, eventually transforming into a vital beacon of safety, liberation and eutopia for LGBTQ+ youth across the country. After its inaugural session in the summer of 1993 and many more held at different campsites across the country, Camp One Heartland found its permanent residence in Willow River, Minnesota. Over the next three decades it broadened its reach to provide summer camp sessions for youth experiencing housing instability, LGBTQ+ youth, and specifically trans youth. Tye attended Camp One Heartland as both a camper in 2022 and a counselor in 2024, and found these experiences indescribably transformative to them and their queer identity. Quite suddenly, Camp One Heartland shut down permanently in the fall of 2024 due to financial issues. Former campers, counselors and staff have been unable to return to the site since. While camp counseling in the summer of 2024, Tye took hundreds of photos of the camp, its people, and its experiences. These serve as some of the last images taken during the lifetime of Camp One Heartland. Artist Bio: Tye DuSold-O’Connor is a multimedia artist studying Fine Art and Psychology whose work revolves around trans experience, identity and culture. events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.

Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. events.title: Charlie Parr
events.description: Charlie Parr, a Duluth-based guitarist and folk troubadour, delivers what Rolling Stone calls "a gritty blend of Delta blues and Depression-era roots music soaked in his hardscrabble voice," and NPR praises as "expertly picked resonator guitar and lyrics that puncture the soul." Over two-and-a-half decades, Parr has released twenty albums while performing up to 275 shows a year at tastemaker events like Newport Folk Fest and Pickathon. A continuer of folk tradition, Parr's sound draws from Folkways legends like Lead Belly and Woody Guthrie, imbued with blues and folk echoes of decades past. His music is shaped by his working-class Minnesota upbringing and Depression-era stories from his father. His 2021 Smithsonian Folkways debut Last of the Better Days Ahead foregrounded his lyrical craftsmanship and bluesman confidence with spare production elevating his blues poetry. His 2024 release Little Sun wove together stories celebrating music, community, and nature into an ambitious, raw album exemplifying his blend of blues and folk traditions with poetic originality. His 2026 album Rooming House joins the chorus of WPA-era socially conscious folk operas and outlaw country concept albums, poignantly allegorizing his experiences and those around him. Jammin' Java welcomes him to Fairfax County, Virginia.

The Duluth-based guitarist, songwriter, and interpreter of traditional music has released twenty albums over two-and-a-half decades and has been known to perform up to 275 shows a year. The sounds from his working-class upbringing—including Folkways legends such as Lead Belly and Woody Guthrie—imbue Parr’s music with stylistic echoes of blues and folk icons of decades past. Parr sees himself merely as a continuer of a folk tradition. Watson will discuss "Deaminative Cross-Couplings." Seminar Details The ubiquity of alkyl amines and the ease of their synthesis makes them attractive precursors fora variety of transformations. In contrast to their classical use as starting materials for complex nitrogen-containing products, we have developed a suite of deaminative methods to convert primary amino groups (NH2) into various carbon substituents via Katritzky pyridinium saltintermediates. events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. events.title: Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY
events.description: For Freedoms presents artist and educator Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY which centers on Ethiopian journalist and author Baalu Girma’s controversial 1984 Amharic novel Oromay, written under the Derg regime and banned shortly after its publication. Drawing on Gottesman’s deep engagement with the novel, NIGHT AND DAY considers how artists create, communicate, and sustain cultural memory within and against conditions of censorship, political repression, and state violence. The exhibition extends beyond the gallery through a library of banned books, a self-guided workshop station that invites visitors to respond to censorship through writing and drawing, and a public conversation on how artists sustain creative practice amid sociopolitical pressure.

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.title: Jazz 4 Justice™
events.venue: George Mason Center for the Arts, Concert Hall
events.description: Join us as we celebrate the 25th Anniversary of Jazz4Justice™, an award-winning partnership between the George Mason University Jazz Program and Northern Virginia's legal community. For a quarter century, Jazz4Justice has demonstrated the power of music to unite communities, raise awareness of the justice gap, and support access to civil legal services for those who cannot afford an attorney. Recognized by the legal profession and honored with George Mason University's Jack Wood Award for Town-Gown Collaboration, Jazz4Justice has become a model for meaningful community engagement. In partnership with Legal Services of Northern Virginia, proceeds from this concert help provide free civil legal assistance to low-income individuals and families facing issues such as housing, domestic violence, consumer protection, family law, veterans' services, and public benefits. Through volunteer attorneys and dedicated legal advocates, LSNV works every day to help ensure that justice is not determined by one's ability to pay. The evening will feature the George Mason Jazz Program performing swinging classics from the golden age of the big band, celebrating both the enduring spirit of jazz and the remarkable partnership that has helped strengthen our community for twenty-five years. events.title: JM Stevens
events.description: 5:00pm • Suggested $10 - $20 donation JM Stevens Austin-based singer-songwriter JM Stevens brings a lifetime of road-worn stories, memorable melodies, and unvarnished honesty to the stage. A former frontman of the longtime SXSW favorite Moonlight Towers, Stevens has built a powerful solo catalog rooted in thoughtful songwriting, acoustic guitar, harmonica, and a voice that feels equally at home in a quiet listening room or a late-night roadhouse. His latest album, Wish on a River Bridge , is a stripped-down and deeply personal collection shaped by the miles between shows. Recorded largely by Stevens at East Austin Recording, the album finds him exploring old beginnings, fresh starts, and all the uncertain territory in between. With echoes of heartland rock, folk, and American roots music, the songs favor emotional truth over ornament—leaving nowhere to hide and plenty to feel. Released in March 2025 on Stevens’ own Crosstie Records, Wish on a River Bridge takes its title from a childhood family tradition: holding your breath and making a wish while crossing a bridge. It’s a fitting image for an artist whose music is full of memory, motion, and hope for what lies ahead. For this show, expect an intimate evening of original songs, road-tested storytelling, and the kind of direct, soulful performance that rewards close listening. JM Stevens • YouTube Channel

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.description: 8 performances | Oct. 31 and Nov. 6*, 7, 13 & 14 at 7:30 p.m. | Nov. 1, 8 & 15 at 2 p.m. Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving, and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four, working in a service job for a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child, but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. Caroline, or Change, produces a valuable theatrical experience that continues to thrill audiences the world over. It is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. The tour will last approximately 1.5 hours. Walking shoes and water are highly recommended. The tour will take place rain or shine. Tickets are $25 per person and include one coffee drink of your choice. Questions? Please e-mail contact@leefendallhouse.org or call the museum at (703) 548-1789. We recommend getting to Cherry on Top at least 10 minutes in advance in order to get your coffee drink and begin the tour at 10:30am.

events.description: Sweeping Promises was born in a disused and reverberant concrete laboratory in Cambridge, MA. Tracked with a self-devised “single-mic technique” and mixed in mono, serial band-starters Lira Mondal and CauField Schnug completed their debut, Hunger for a Way Out, just in time to enter quarantine. With only a single basement show under their belt, the band received an unexpectedly wide reception, Firstly in online punk circles, and eventually stretching beyond. In 2023, having gotten the chance to tour the USA and abroad with live drummer Spenser Gralla, the duo relocated to their new home and DIY recording compound in Lawrence, KS, and released their sophomore album, Good Living is Coming for You, on Feel It Records (US) and Sub Pop (EU/UK). events.title: Unfossilizing African Art
events.description: Presented after extensive research, this exhibition recontextualizes African material culture objects held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. events.title: Yoga Philosophy & History - $295
events.description: OVERVIEW: Yoga philosophy isn’t just abstract ideas—it’s a roadmap to a more complete understanding of ourselves and our world. Studying yoga philosophy allows you to implement its wisdom, not just think about it. This module is designed to provide serious yoga practitioners with a clear understanding of how the yoga tradition has developed over time and support yoga teachers who want to infuse their classes with yoga philosophy's timeless wisdom. FRIDAY, 12:00 - 3:00 PM: Yoga from a Historical Perspective — The historical development of Vedic schools of thought and yogic practices on the Indian subcontinent, Vedic culture and Buddhism, an overview of the Vedas, Upanishads, Puranas, the Vedanta-sutra, and later Hatha and Tantric texts, Vedic epistemology (how to know what is worthy of belief), and the three categories of knowledge in the Vedic system. FRIDAY, 3:30 - 6:30 PM: Yoga from a Transcendental Perspective — The origins of yoga according to the tradition itself, the underlying metaphysics and creation theory of Vedic yoga philosophy, how the basic philosophical premises of yoga compare with conventional modern wisdom, the five functions of yoga philosophy, and the way to understand yoga philosophy according to yoga philosophy itself. events.title: 1776, the Musical, presented by The Pickwick Players
events.description: Virginia helped shape the beginnings of our nation, and local audiences can experience the drama, humor and music behind America’s founding in 1776 , the Tony Award-winning musical presented by The Pickwick Players. Just in time for America’s 250th anniversary, 1776 takes audiences inside the Continental Congress, where John Adams pushes for independence, Benjamin Franklin brings his wit and wisdom, and Virginia’s own Thomas Jefferson is called upon to put the revolutionary cause into words. The story also features Richard Henry Lee of Virginia, whose resolution calling for independence helped move the colonies toward a historic decision. What happens when a room full of passionate, stubborn and politically divided men try to agree on the future of a nation? There’s plenty of debate, a little scheming, larger-than-life personalities and some unforgettable music. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 combines clever dialogue, colorful characters, political maneuvering and a memorable score. From the spirited opening number, “Sit Down, John,” to the lively “The Lees of Old Virginia” and the stirring “Is Anybody There?,” the music captures the humor, frustrations and high stakes behind the birth of a nation. Forget the dusty history books. 1776 presents the founding fathers as real people, with big egos, strong opinions, competing interests and a monumental decision to make. events.description: Yang 24 is a short, flowing tai chi sequence practiced slowly with smooth weight shifts, relaxed joints, and an upright spine. This style incorporates basic martial arts movements while keeping the practitioner in a relaxed state of mind. Eight Brocades (Ba Duan Jin) is a set of eight simple qigong movements that coordinate gentle stretching with calm breathing. In this practice, you are moving in specific ways to bring energy (qi) within the energy lines (meridians) to bring harmony within the body. Practiced together, they feel like a blend of “moving meditation” and whole-body maintenance. You can expect to spend time repeating movements to refine alignment, soften tension, and improve coordination. The effort level is usually light to moderate, with a focus on ease rather than strain. Early sessions often bring a noticeable sense of calm and a loosening of shoulders, hips, and back. With consistent practice, many people find that daily movement feels smoother and steadier, especially when standing, walking, or changing direction. Benefits build gradually and are strongest when you stay relaxed, breathe comfortably, and practice within your current range of motion. You may begin to become sensitive to energy (qi) within and around your body. - Balance and stability: Better control during weight shifting, stepping, and turning. - Mobility and flexibility: A gentler, more comfortable range of motion in the hips, spine, shoulders, and ankles. - Leg strength and posture: Stron

events.title: A Gift in Motion
events.description: A multidisciplinary showcase from the artists and scholars of the full-time faculty and staff at the Corcoran School of the Arts & Design. A Gift In Motion loosely draws from Robin Wall Kimmerer’s book The Serviceberry which uplifts Indigenous frameworks of the natural world to advance the possibilities in collectivity, reciprocity, and the mindset of abundance. These are anti-capitalist models and theories that provide insight into the systems of power we negotiate, but also offer a lens on how we individually move through our daily lives—together—through historically fraught landscapes. A keen reminder that working with, for, and because of each other remains the most human motivation, even while we are inundated with narratives that suggest otherwise. Within the walls of the academy, frameworks of artistic and creative knowledge are often dismissed, as are Indigenous methodologies and community-focused perspectives that center human engagement, oral and craft-based practices, and unquantifiable research. A personal experience. A feeling. Abstraction. And yet, for centuries, within the walls of art schools exist myriad economies of imagination that are anchored in the sharing of diverse creative knowledge and articulated in what we make, write, perform, dance, build, conserve, collect, display, speak, and think. We do this all—in small and grand gestures, every day— in service of learning with and for each other in the crafting of the world we wish to see. Perhaps we are ar

events.title: Adam Ezra Group
events.description: Jammin' Java welcomes Adam Ezra Group on Thursday, November 14th, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. at 227 Maple Avenue in Vienna, Fairfax County, Virginia. Over more than two decades of relentless grassroots touring, Adam Ezra Group has built something far bigger than a typical touring band: a fiercely independent, fan-powered community that expands one show at a time. Rooms across the country sell out when Adam Ezra Group comes to town, with longtime fans regularly traveling across state lines to catch multiple shows, drawn by the band's deep sense of community and the promise that no two nights are ever the same. The band never performs from a fixed setlist; instead, they shape each night around the energy in the room. Songs, stories, and moments unfold in real time—part concert, part revival, and part reminder of what live music can still be at its best. Blending folk/Americana soul, rock 'n' roll energy, and deeply human songwriting, Adam Ezra Group has built one of the most authentic underground followings in live music today while quickly becoming recognized on a national level. SPIN describes them as "an independent underground folk band blowing up without selling out," a rise powered entirely by word of mouth, community activism, and genuine connection between band and audience that turns first-time listeners into lifelong fans. Catch them now while they're still playing intimate rooms where you can give Adam a hug on your way out. Adam Ezra Group delivers authentic artistry, community spirit, and unforgettable live music in Fairfax County, Virginia. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: Aging Well: You Rest, You Rust With Dr. Patrice Winter
events.description: Aging well is not a spectator sport. Our bodies are designed for movement. Our bodies begin aging as soon as we stop growing in our early 20s. Learn about joints. What is normal, what is not? How can we assist joint health through movement, posture and exercise? Be an active participant in your healthy future. We will begin from where you are now physically. If you have limited motion in a joint(s), need an assistive device or have no physical complaints and want to stay that way, this talk is for you. We will address the strategies on how to do this with flare. Wear comfortable shoes and clothes you can move freely in. Dr. Patrice Winter, PT, DPT, MHA, FAAOMPT, is a retired professor from George Mason University’s College of Public Health, Department of Global and Community Health, where she taught health-related curriculum with emphasis in public health, disease, healthy living and aging well. Dr. Winter practiced physical therapy for over 35 years and was a spokesperson for the American Physical Therapy Association for almost twenty years.

It was a gratifying moment she did not take for granted. Qi had overcome a viral WeChat disinformation campaign from her Chinese community and was met with skepticism from the Democratic establishment before being elected. Unfossilizing African Art recontextualizes African material culture objects that have been held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students across four seminar courses conducted original research to deepen understanding of the collection and reconsider how these objects are interpreted and exhibited. events.title: Camp One Heartland
events.description: Camp One Heartland is a solo exhibition by Tye DuSold-O’Connor archiving documentation of one of the world’s first nonprofit summer camps designated to supporting and empowering youth affected by HIV and AIDS, eventually transforming into a vital beacon of safety, liberation and eutopia for LGBTQ+ youth across the country. After its inaugural session in the summer of 1993 and many more held at different campsites across the country, Camp One Heartland found its permanent residence in Willow River, Minnesota. Over the next three decades it broadened its reach to provide summer camp sessions for youth experiencing housing instability, LGBTQ+ youth, and specifically trans youth. Tye attended Camp One Heartland as both a camper in 2022 and a counselor in 2024, and found these experiences indescribably transformative to them and their queer identity. Quite suddenly, Camp One Heartland shut down permanently in the fall of 2024 due to financial issues. Former campers, counselors and staff have been unable to return to the site since. While camp counseling in the summer of 2024, Tye took hundreds of photos of the camp, its people, and its experiences. These serve as some of the last images taken during the lifetime of Camp One Heartland. Artist Bio: Tye DuSold-O’Connor is a multimedia artist studying Fine Art and Psychology whose work revolves around trans experience, identity and culture. events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.

Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. Image: Boris Ignatovich (Russian, 1899-1976), Composer Dmitri Shostakovich, from "Ignatovich, Soviet Avant-Garde", 1928, gelatin silver print, 16 H x 20 W in. events.title: Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY
events.description: For Freedoms presents artist and educator Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY which centers on Ethiopian journalist and author Baalu Girma’s controversial 1984 Amharic novel Oromay, written under the Derg regime and banned shortly after its publication. Drawing on Gottesman’s deep engagement with the novel, NIGHT AND DAY considers how artists create, communicate, and sustain cultural memory within and against conditions of censorship, political repression, and state violence. The exhibition extends beyond the gallery through a library of banned books, a self-guided workshop station that invites visitors to respond to censorship through writing and drawing, and a public conversation on how artists sustain creative practice amid sociopolitical pressure.

events.description: Step back in time and explore the tastes, traditions, and stories that shaped colonial Annapolis! This immersive walking tour reveals how food reflected class, culture, trade, and daily life. Visit three distinctive historic sites: the Waterfront Warehouse, Hogshead Trades Museum, and William Paca House & Garden. Along the way, discover how global trade, local ingredients, social status, and enslavement shaped what Annapolitans ate and how food was prepared and served. Explore the everyday foodways of working and middling residents, the elaborate dining customs of the city’s elite, and the essential labor and culinary knowledge of enslaved people. events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

What Awaits You: What Makes This Experience Unique: A beautifully styled luxury fall picnic surrounded by the peaceful beauty of the farm Cozy charcuterie boards filled with handcrafted seasonal bites from Graze & Savor A s’mores and cider station to keep you warm and nostalgic Sweet, slow moments brushing, feeding, and connecting with our gentle Highland cows A simple, creative Highland cow craft to take a piece of the magic home Intentional space to slow down, connect, and savor the season This isn’t just a picnic — it’s a celebration of everything we love about fall: comfort, community, and the joy of being present. Tickets limited to ensure an intimate, relaxed experience, and advance tickets are required. This event is for adults and children ages 10 and up.

events.title: Lez Zeppelin: The Song Remains The Same - 50th Anniversary Celebration
events.address: 220 N. Washington Street, Falls Church, VA 22046
events.description: Lez Zeppelin celebrates 50 years of Led Zeppelin at The State Theatre on Saturday, November 14th, 2026. Doors open at 7:00 p.m. with showtime at 8:30 p.m. Founded in 2004 by New York guitarist Steph Paynes, this all-girl quartet has gained unanimous critical acclaim as one of the most exciting live acts around, becoming the first female rock act to pay homage to Led Zeppelin while garnering rave reviews worldwide. Lez Zeppelin stays true to the musically audacious spirit of the original, delivering Led Zeppelin's blistering arrangements and monstrous sound note-for-note at sold-out shows globally. In June 2013, Jimmy Page attended their London show and said of the group: "they played the led zeppelin music with an extraordinary sensuality and an energy and passion that highlighted their superb musicianship." What sets Lez Zeppelin apart is their seamless, unique injection of gender-bending performance into the original material. Featured on major television including BBC, CNN, ABC, CBS, MTV, VH-1, and Fox, plus radio shows like Sirius XM and NPR, their first studio album was produced by legendary Eddie Kramer (Led Zeppelin, Jimi Hendrix). Their second LP, Lez Zeppelin I, authentically remakes Led Zeppelin's debut using the same vintage equipment from 1968. From 40,000-person performances at Times Square to Bonnaroo, Hellfest, and the Isle of Wight, plus twice at Madison Square Garden, Lez Zeppelin has broken both glass and class ceilings. Tickets are $30 advance or $34 day of show. Attendees must be 18 or older to enter unless accompanied by a parent; valid ID is required. Lez Zeppelin offers far more than a tribute—it's a transformative celebration of classic rock excellence at The State Theatre in the Fairfax County area, Virginia. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: NATIONAL PARKS ALONG THE POTOMAC
events.description: What: Four Mile Ranger Guided History Hike from the Carousel in Glen Echo Park to the C&O Canal National Historical Park, Union Arch Bridge and the Clara Barton NHS When: 9:30am Starting Point: The Dentzel Carousel at Glen Echo Park, 7300 MacArthur Blvd. Glen Echo, MD 20812 This two and half hour, four-mile guided hike starts at the Carousel in Glen Echo Park. We will walk through the park and uncover the story of what was once Washington’s premiere amusement park. Next, we will walk a rough downhill trail and cross over the C&O Canal where we will learn about African American canal worker, George Pointer. We will then walk up-stream before crossing the canal again and ascending the hill to learn about the Union Arch Bridge, part of the Washington Aqueduct. Finally, we will stroll through the town of Glen Echo to Clara Barton National Historic Site (NHS) where we will discover the history of the house and the story of its famous resident, the founder of the American Red Cross, Clara Barton. events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Opera: Così fan tutte
events.description: Dive into the wit and wonder of human comedy with "MainStage Series: Così fan tutte" on November 14, 2026, at 7:00 PM. One night only, prepare to be swept away by Mozart's ingenious work, brought to life in a captivating semi-staged concert production. This exquisite presentation, accompanied by live orchestra, will delight families of all ages and is a great way to get to know one of the finest works in the operatic repertoire. Two confident young soldiers wager that their fiancées could never be unfaithful — and to prove it, they disguise themselves and set out to woo each other's bride. What follows is Mozart's wickedly funny, achingly beautiful meditation on love, loyalty, and the games we play with the heart. Così fan tutte ("So do they all") sparkles with some of the most gorgeous ensembles ever written, wrapping its sly comedy around music of startling tenderness. By the final curtain, no one is quite who they thought they were — and everyone has learned that the heart is far more complicated than any bet can settle.

Hikes are limited to 30 visitors each and first-come, first-serve free tickets for the hike will be available at the event at Cabin Camp 2 starting at 8:30am. events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Rockville Musical Theatre presents “Caroline, or Change”
events.description: 8 performances | Oct. 31 and Nov. 6*, 7, 13 & 14 at 7:30 p.m. | Nov. 1, 8 & 15 at 2 p.m. Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving, and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four, working in a service job for a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child, but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. Caroline, or Change, produces a valuable theatrical experience that continues to thrill audiences the world over. It is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers for the better. Featuring one of the most powerful female roles in musi

events.title: Roosevelt at Rock Creek Park
events.description: Lace up your hiking boots and follow in the footsteps of Theodore Roosevelt, the adventurous president who believed that time spent in nature built character, courage, and a stronger nation. Beginning at Peirce Mill, this 1.5-mile (round-trip) guided hike winds through scenic trails and rugged landscapes that Roosevelt explored while escaping the pressures of the presidency. This hike covers uneven, tight, rocky terrain with steep elevation changes and may be challenging for some visitors. Participants should wear sturdy footwear, bring water, and dress appropriately for the weather. Recommended for ages 10 and older. Children must be accompanied by an adult.

events.title: Seth Walker
events.description: Seth Walker brings his soulful blend of Blues, Americana, and Roots music to the stage with the easy groove and gospel‑rich vocals that have made him a standout in today’s roots scene. Currently celebrating his new album Why The Worry , Walker leans into a philosophy of ease and authenticity, channeling influences from JJ Cale to Bill Withers and Al Green. The album reunites him with longtime collaborators and features a mix of originals and carefully chosen covers that reflect resilience, warmth, and a renewed musical clarity. Praised by NPR, American Songwriter, and The Washington Post, Walker has toured with The Mavericks, The Wood Brothers, Raul Malo, and Ruthie Foster. His songwriting continues to reach new audiences, including “Moon and Stars,” the title track of The Mavericks’ recent album. With twelve albums, a signature blend of melody and groove, and a sound that feels both timeless and freshly inspired, Seth Walker offers an unforgettable live experience, equal parts soulful, uplifting, and deeply human.

events.title: Sweet Dreams: Mandy Barnett Sings Patsy Cline
events.description: “Sweet Dreams” is a stunning tribute to the timeless music of Patsy Cline. The concert features a collection of iconic classic country songs originally recorded by Patsy Cline, including “Crazy,” “Sweet Dreams,” “Walking After Midnight,” “I Fall to Pieces,” “Always,” “Faded Love,” “She’s Got You,” “Strange,” and many more. Widely considered Nashville’s finest vocalist, Mandy Barnett rose to prominence at the age of 18 after being chosen among 400 auditionees by the legendary Ryman Auditorium for the title role in the 1994 musical production of Always… Patsy Cline . Her successful performance as Patsy Cline garnered tremendous press, both domestic and international, establishing the production as a staple of American theater. An official member of the Grand Ole Opry since 2021, Mandy has performed on more than 400 occasions, sharing the stage with legendary performers including Dolly Parton, Ringo Starr, Kristin Chenoweth, Pat Benatar, Judy Collins, Connie Stevens, Garth Brooks, and Michael Feinstein, among numerous others. Learn more about “Sweet Dreams” and Mandy Barnett by visiting her official website. This show is part of the Weinberg Center’s Centennial Events, celebrating 100 years of entertainment in our historic building. The Weinberg Center , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers a historic backdrop and timeless atmosphere for a meaningful entertainment experience.

events.title: The Shape of the Universe
events.description: Have you ever looked up at a beautiful clear dark starlit night, and wondered whether space goes on forever? Or is there an edge, a boundary where it stops? Astronomers know that distant galaxies are rushing away from our own Milky Way, and think that the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago - called the "big bang" but really tiny. What will the universe be like in "deep time"? Completely empty (or full of dark energy) or will it collapse down to a "big crunch" or neither? Join us for a discussion on these questions with physicist and author Dr. Michael Albrow.

events.title: Unfossilizing African Art
events.description: Presented after extensive research, this exhibition recontextualizes African material culture objects held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. Image: Once Known Mende carver [Mende, Sierra Leone], Sowei, 19th-20th century, wood, varnish, 16 H x 10 W x 10 D in. Gift of Stephen A. Spear, 1975 (P.75.2.30)

events.title: Weekend Unwind: Sound Bath + Reiki : Saturday Mornings in Falls Church
events.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
events.description: Most people start their Saturday with a list. Groceries, errands, the thing they didn't finish on Friday, still buzzing around in their head. By the time they've “relaxed,” it's Sunday night. Weekend Unwind flips that. Eleven o'clock, one hour, lying down. Crystal singing bowls, a short guided meditation, and Reiki, in a small room with ten people in it and no agenda at all. Nothing to achieve, nothing to be good at. You just lie there and let the week drain out of your shoulders. This class has a different feel from our Thursday night one. Thursday is about switching off. Saturday is slower. People arrive less wound up, settle in faster, and tend to float out rather than rush out. Several regulars come as their standing Saturday thing, the way other people have a standing brunch. It pairs well with brunch afterwards, for the record. If you've never been to a sound bath: you keep your clothes on, you lie on a mat under a blanket, you close your eyes, and I do the rest. The bowls are played around and near you, the sound is physical as much as it is musical, you feel it in your chest, and an hour passes faster than you expect. Everything is provided. Show up in something comfortable with ten minutes to spare, and that's the whole preparation. I'm Victoria Vita. I've been a CPA for over twenty years and a healer for more than seven, and I teach every one of these classes myself. When you come back, and most people do, it's the same room, the same bowls, and the same person. That sameness is kind of the point. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Guests mention the warm welcome, feeling comfortable from the first visit, and booking again — that's the Saturday I try to run. What's included: • 60 minutes of crystal singing bowls, guided meditation and Reiki • Mat, blanket and bolster provided... just bring yourself • Ten spots only, so the room stays quiet and unhurried • A slow finish... no one is hustled out the door at noon Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: YOUR Body in Yoga: A Functional Anatomy Weekend with Machelle Lee
events.address: 30 W. Potomac St., Ste 102, Brunswick, MD 21716
events.description: Harshly judging one's range of motion is one of the greatest sources of unnecessary suffering in many people’s yoga practice. The poses in yoga are intended to be a method to move the regenerative and healing life force. To do that effectively in yoga, we must understand each of our own (or our students) unique structures and explore when we can move more deeply into a posture or when to acknowledge limitations with respect. Although some restrictions in range of motion are related to tight muscles, and more are related to contracted fascia and ligaments, many significant limitations are actually due to variations in bone shapes and joint orientations that can differ dramatically from one person to the next. Understanding YOUR yoga anatomy is best learned through direct hands-on experience - testing your bones/joints and witnessing them curiously and compassionately to the bones of others. This functional, comparative anatomy workshop explores the 14 major joint segments of the body that account for most of our yoga postures. For each joint intersection, we will perform bone analysis and range of motion tests on ourselves, compare with each other, and demonstrate how each varying joints will express itself in specific yoga postures. 12 CEUs Available for Yoga Teachers with Yoga Alliance Anatomy is a vast subject, but this interactive workshop reveals the basics in a way that clarifies and simplifies the yoga practice - putting the attention back where it belongs - how the key action of each pose makes you FEEL and moves the life force. In this workshop, participants often experience an “ah-ha” moment about their body and their practice, which can be powerfully liberating and self-accepting. This workshop is ideal for all yoga practitioners, whether one is a beginner or experienced student wishing to deepen their knowledge of their body in practice and for yoga teachers looking to expand their teaching and cueing.

events.title: A Call to Chapel with the Rev. Brandon Crawley Thomas, Ph.D. (in-person and virtual)
events.description: The Reverend Brandon Thomas Crowley, Ph.D., is a pastor, author, scholar, and public intellectual whose research explores Black religious thought, theology, ecclesiology, and social ethics from the late 19th through the early 21st centuries. Since 2009, he has served as Senior Pastor of the Historic Myrtle Baptist Church in Newton, Massachusetts, a congregation founded by formerly enslaved Africans during Reconstruction and widely known for its inclusive ministry and commitment to social justice. In addition to his pastoral leadership, Dr. Crowley has taught at Harvard University, Emory University, Boston University, the Episcopal Theological Seminary of the Southwest, and other institutions. His debut book, Queering Black Churches: Dismantling Heteronormativity in African American Congregations, was published by Oxford University Press in 2024. To learn more about our guest speaker, click here.

events.title: Camelot
events.description: Welcome to CAMELOT! Borrowing from the Arthurian legends, CAMELOT is Lerner and Loewe's fantastical masterpiece. An idealistic King Arthur hopes to create a kingdom built on honor and dignity, embodied by his Knights of The Round Table. He establishes an order built on using “might for right.” His ideals, however, are tested when his lovely queen, Guenevere, falls in love with his most loyal knight, Lancelot. Add in the dastardly Mordred and his wicked schemes and it soon appears this dream of a kingdom may only exist for one brief, shining moment. ​ This stirring Golden Age musical has enchanted generations of theatregoers with its sweeping score and iconic characters. It is a romance, a tragedy, a comedy, an adventure, a fantasy, and a stirring exploration of power and leadership all at once. And above all, it is a piece about the stories and ideals we pass along to future generations.​

events.description: 8 performances | October 31 and November 6*, 7, 13, and 14 at 7:30pm | November 1, 8, and 15 at 2:00pm *Friday, November 6 will include ASL interpretation and free tickets for Montgomery County residents! Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.title: Mary M. Lane, author of Hitler's Last Hostages
events.description: Join local Virginia author Mary M. Lane to discuss her critically acclaimed book, Hitler's last hostages: looted art and the soul of the Third Reich . The book was one of three finalists for the Commonwealth of Virginia’s Book of the Year in 2020. In 2012, the German government confiscated roughly 1,300 works by Heni Matisse, George Grosz, Claude Monet, and other masters from the apartment of Cornelius Gurlitt, the reclusive son of one of Hitler's primary art dealers — Hildebrand Gurlitt. For two years, the government kept the discovery a secret. In Hitler's Last Hostages , Mary M. Lane reveals the fate of those works and tells the definitive story of art in the Third Reich and Germany's ongoing struggle to right the wrongs of the past. Copies of the book will be available for purchase and signing.

events.title: Maryland Winds – In a Nutshell
events.description: Our 2026–27 season, Epic Works, showcases four remarkable large-scale compositions that demonstrate the depth, imagination, and expressive power of the wind band repertoire. Each concert features a major multi-movement work as its centerpiece, while remaining true to the Maryland Winds tradition of offering audiences a rich and diverse musical experience throughout the season. Our second featured work is Percy Grainger’s In a Nutshell , the celebrated four-movement suite first performed in 1916. In just twenty minutes, Grainger captures the rhythmic vitality, folk-inspired melodies, and inventive orchestration that define his unmistakable compositional voice. Compact in length but expansive in imagination, the work remains one of the great masterpieces of the wind band repertoire. https://marylandwinds.com/season.html Sunday, November 15th, 2026 at 3:00 pm Guilford Park High School Auditorium 8500 Ridgelys Run Road Jessup, MD 20794 https://app.arts-people.com/index.php?show=355760 $20 – General Admission $17 – Seniors (65+) $10 – Students Maryland Winds is an ensemble of professional musicians in the greater Baltimore–Washington, DC, area. events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.description: Petals & Poses Join us for a cozy morning of stretch, wine, and flower arranging as we celebrate the fall season at Petals and Poses! Help us celebrate the season of gathering and friendship at the winery with a relaxing morning of yoga, floral arranging, and wine! Awaken your senses, calm your mind, and reconnect with your body and your community in this soul-nourishing event. Start the morning with a beginner-friendly yoga practice led by local pro Rhonda Wilson in our historic heartstone barn — focusing on breath, body awareness, and gentle movement to release tension, build strength, and constructive rest. Throughout this stretch to release focused practice, you’ll be prompted to participate in “let go” and allow your inner artist blossom. Please bring a yoga mat and a blanket, arrive by 9:45 AM, and layer up for comfort. Warm socks, a blanket, and water are also recommended! After yoga, dive into a hands-on floral arranging workshop with Angela Rabena of Blooms2u. events.title: Rockville Musical Theatre presents “Caroline, or Change”
events.description: 8 performances | Oct. 31 and Nov. 6*, 7, 13 & 14 at 7:30 p.m. | Nov. 1, 8 & 15 at 2 p.m. Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving, and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four, working in a service job for a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child, but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. Caroline, or Change, produces a valuable theatrical experience that continues to thrill audiences the world over. It is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. events.title: So Others May Live: Army Aeromedical Evacuation Operations in the Republic of Vietnam, 1962-1973
events.venue: National Museum of Health and Medicine
events.description: During the Vietnam War, “Dustoff” became the name for helicopter medical evacuation missions that transformed battlefield medicine. Beginning with the first five Huey helicopters deployed to Vietnam, unarmed Dustoff crews evacuated more than 900,000 wounded and injured between 1962 and 1973. Their work helped wounded service members reach lifesaving care within the critical “golden hour” after injury. Join Donald Hall, Ph.D., as he explores the history, innovation, and lasting impact of Dustoff and the evolution of battlefield medical evacuation during the Vietnam War.

events.title: The Catholic University of America Symphony Orchestra in Concert
events.venue: St. Andrew the Apostle Catholic Church
events.description: On Sunday, November 15, at 4:00 PM, the St. Andrew the Apostle Concert Series proudly welcomes The Catholic University of America Symphony Orchestra, conducted by Maestro Simeone Tartaglione, for a free afternoon of orchestral masterworks. Program Paul Dukas – The Sorcerer’s Apprentice Camille Saint-Saëns – Cello Concerto No. 1 in A minor Vasily Popov, cello Camille Saint-Saëns – Symphony No. 3 in C minor, “Organ Symphony” Michael Murphy, organ The centerpiece is Saint-Saëns’ thrilling Organ Symphony, which integrates the pipe organ into two of its four movements for a powerful blend of orchestral color and majestic organ sound. Performing on the St. Andrew Pipe Organ of the Holy Archangels—a French Romantic instrument installed by the Peragallo Pipe Organ Company in 2020 (three manuals, 51 ranks, 2,891 pipes)—organist Michael Murphy will bring the work’s full intended glory to life. The program opens with Dukas’ vivid symphonic poem, famously featured in Disney’s Fantasia, followed by one of the most beloved cello concertos of the 19th century. This concert is ideal for anyone who appreciates masterful composition, virtuoso performance, and the transcendent beauty of live symphonic music in a sacred setting. About the Conductor Maestro Simeone Tartaglione is Associate Professor of Practice in Instrumental Music at The Catholic University of America’s Rome School of Performing Arts, where he serves as Conducting Area Head and conductor of the university orchestra. Trained in the European tradition at Rome’s Santa Cecilia Conservatory and with advanced degrees including a Doctorate in Philology, he has conducted across Europe, the United States, South Africa, and beyond. He currently serves as Music Director of the Newark Symphony Orchestra and Delaware Youth Symphony, among others. He is the recipient of the prestigious 2025 Telamone Prize. events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.description: The 2026 U.S. midterm elections and Taiwan’s 2026 local elections unfold during landmark democratic anniversaries: the United States’ semiquincentennial and the 30th anniversary of Taiwan’s first direct presidential election. These parallel milestones provide a unique lens for examining how democratic identity, institutional resilience, and cross‑Strait geopolitics shape electoral behavior in both polities. In the United States, midterm dynamics reflect heightened economic anxieties, rising consumer prices, shifting partisan narratives, and growing voter concerns over affordability and foreign policy crises, including the conflict with Iran. Simultaneously, Taiwan’s local elections occur amid intensified political competition, partisan division, heightened public and legislative debate on issues such as defense spending, and renewed attention to democratic consolidation and public trust. U.S.–Taiwan relations increasingly intersect with both electoral contexts. In Washington, bipartisan congressional resolutions reaffirm support for Taiwan’s democratic resilience and highlight growing concern over coercive pressure from the PRC. In Taiwan, cross‑Strait tensions, security and economic relations with the United States, and China’s influence operations—including AI‑driven disinformation—shape public discourse and electoral priorities. events.description: Experiencing history through outdoor mindfulness at Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House. About the Session: The sessions are approximately 90-minutes long and are conducted in relative silence. They include warm-ups, centering, and breathing exercises to connect participants to their bodies and the world around them. These are followed by a walk and an extended sit which encourages participants to become more fully open and present to their surroundings. We conclude with a returning ritual and a chance to reflect on the experience. This time in nature will not be strenuous; most abilities can be accommodated. All ages are welcomed but children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult. Important Arrival & Check-In Details Check-In Location: All participants must check in at Woodlawn, regardless of session topic. Timing: Sessions start promptly at 12:00 PM (Sundays). Please arrive early to ensure a timely start. Duration: Approximately 90 minutes. events.description: Did you know that part of the Washington-Rochambeau Revolutionary Route National Historic Trail passes through Prince William Forest Park? Take a hike through history at Prince William Forest Park on the Crossing Trail, which follows part of the route where, in 1781, General Rochambeau's French Army and General Washington's Continental Army marched troops south from New York to fight the British Army in Yorktown, VA during the Revolutionary War. Celebrate the 250th anniversary of American Independence by following in the footsteps of these armies as you learn about travel in the 1700s along this one and a half mile trail. Bring water and bug spray on this mostly shaded one and a half hour hike.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape. Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available. Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape.Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available.Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Explore a little-known part of the park and tour a cabin camp built in the 1930s. Join park rangers at Cabin Camp 2 at Prince William Forest Park to learn more about the period of the park’s history in the 1940s when the Office of Strategic Services (OSS) trained spies in the park. Take a rugged two mile hike off-trail with a ranger to an old OSS training ground at 9:00 am or 12:30pm and/or tour the cabin camp to learn more about the OSS. Hikes are limited to 30 visitors each and first-come, first-serve free tickets for the hike will be available at the event at Cabin Camp 2 starting at 8:30am. Unfortunately, the off-trail hike is inaccessible to wheelchairs and strollers. It is recommended to wear long pants and hiking shoes if planning to do the off-trail hike. Guided cabin camp tours are offered to visitors after each hike and are open to all visitors. Visitors are also welcome to do a self-guided tour of the cabin camp anytime between 8:30am and 3:00pm. The cabin camp gates will close at 3:00pm.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape.Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available.Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Forest Bathing, also known as Forest Therapy, is a slow, mindful immersion in nature that originated in Japan. The guide suggests voluntary activities called invitations that help participants let go of the busyness of everyday life and immerse themselves in the soothing sensuality of nature. This session of Forest Bathing is run by a Virginia Master Naturalist from the Merrimac Farm Chapter. It is recommended that visitors wear long pants and walking shoes and bring water and insect repellant.

events.description: Join a ranger on a walk to learn about Georgetown during one of the most turbulent chapters in American history. From the divided loyalties of Georgetown residents to the presence of Union soldiers, this tour reveals the hidden stories of a community caught between North and South. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring water. This hike will utilize sidewalks that can be narrow and uneven at times. It will traverse nearly two miles of neighborhood streets in the Georgetown area of DC. Additional Information: Tour departs from the Old Stone House There are no public facilities available on this hike. Recommended for ages 12 and up. Walk may be cancelled in the event of bad weather at the discretion of park staff. Feel free to check the Rock Creek Park website the day of to confirm. Or call the Nature Center (202-895-6070) the day of to confirm and be sure to leave a voicemail for a callback.

events.description: Free Concert at St. George’s: Vox Humana VOX HUMANA RICHMOND will perform on Sunday, November 15, at 3:00 for a concert entitled “Of Birds and Flight.” The concert will be in St. George’s Episcopal Church’s historic nave, located at 905 Princess Anne Street in downtown Fredericksburg. The concert program brings together a wide variety of works exploring humanity’s fascination with birds and their ability to fly. The centerpiece, Eric Whitacre’s “Leonardo Dreams of His Flying Machine,” portrays the great Renaissance polymath and his obsession with inventing a birdlike machine that would let him fly. The music ranges widely in style, from Renaissance composer Orlando Gibbons (“The Silver Swan”) to the Beatles (“Blackbird”). Also featured is Pulitzer Prize–winning composer Caroline Shaw, whose setting of Psalm 84 includes the verse “the sparrow has found a house, and the swallow a nest where she may lay her young.” Vox Humana is a twelve-voice choral ensemble of professional singers, based in Richmond, Virginia. Created in 2020, Vox Humana, performs a wide range of music, both sacred and secular, covering various periods of music history and diverse cultures. Known for its lush acoustics and welcoming atmosphere, St. George’s offers a year-round concert series showcasing both local and nationally recognized artists. events.description: Immerse yourself in the daily life of soldiers, military officers, and the camp followers who traveled with the army as you explore a Revolutionary War encampment. See two daily programs about enlisting in General Washington's army and how soldiers prepared their meals while traveling. This attraction is made possible thanks to Americana Corner.
